page: Amazon Web Services r8i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across several compute and memory tasks. The CPU features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and matrix math. Single-threaded gzip compression (33.51 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.21 GB/sec) perform in the top 25%, while Geekbench text processing reaches the top 10% tier at 2828.0. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is measured at 133.67 GB/sec, and write bandwidth is 63.0 GB/sec. For LLM workloads, the instance achieves 404.39 tokens/sec for text generation on a small 135M model and 209.76 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a 7B model, though text generation on larger 70B models drops to a weaker 2.71 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r8i.8xlarge offers a high-density DDR5 memory configuration paired with dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of local storage. The combination of 256 GB of RAM, high-speed memory bandwidth, and strong text and image processing capabilities makes this instance well-suited for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, enterprise applications, and medium-scale data processing pipelines.
